dialogue: Woke up dreading the day, fixed a flat tyre in the rain under some sad excuse for shade, and then the wind tried to throw me into a railing.
Watched a couple actually get blown over on their bikes. Not funny. Okay, a little funny.
Bailed on the north shore plan, ducked inland instead, and got smacked in the face with the most gorgeous plains and farmland view from a hill.
Ended the day flying downhill with the wind at my back, grinning like an idiot. Lake Biwa giveth and taketh.
Rode the Biwaichi path today, lake on one side, mountains and farms on the other, pure serenity.
Detoured up to Hikone Castle, legs were screaming but the view over the lake made it worth every pedal.
Grabbed spare inner tubes at a bike shop so I won't be stranded again, then watched civilisation quietly fade behind me.
Cozy guesthouse, no lock on the door, and a whole lot of countryside silence. Not complaining!
Five days around Lake Biwa and I'm finally back where I started, in Otsu.
Rest day in Takashima first though, my legs were begging after all those flats.
This morning the fog was so thick I couldn't even see across the lake, felt endless.
Now it just feels like a dream. A dream that ends in ramen and gyoza, thankfully.
Parkrun in Otsu at dawn, then straight onto the bike for the last leg back to Osaka. Rookie mistake, honestly.
Every hill today I just got off and walked, legs were absolutely cooked from the run. The downhills into Kyoto made up for it though.
Some guy at a konbini thought I owned this bike. Let him believe it, it's rented but it's MY rental.
Made it to Fukuoka just in time to stop the drink counter reset, saved everyone's night. Now if you'll excuse me, my legs are gone.
Shirakawa-go was unreal, mountains like a green-brown-gold rainbow, snow dusted on the peaks.
Crossed a wobbly stone bridge twice just for katsu and icecream, my heart nearly gave out both times.
Our host lady fed us butter-soft beef and warned us a bear would kill us if we walked at night, love her.
Also I'm now a certified stink bug executioner, tape and all. Ask me anything!
Started the day calm in an onsen overlooking the river, chilly air and all - so peaceful.
Then Kanazawa happened: udon with chain-smoking salary men in an 80s time capsule of a restaurant.
90 minutes all-you-can-drink for $18, seven rounds deep, wagyu that made it all worth it.
Ended up at a whiskey bar trying to buy cigars and accidentally guilt-tripping the poor bartender into giving me cigarettes. Going back for round two.
Day one of biking Lake Biwa, and I nearly left the shop without my helmet!
No offline maps, so I just vibed it along the Yodogawa river toward Ōtsu.
Ended up on the wrong side of the lake and got dumped onto surprise hills, biggest climb of my life, Strava gave me a medal for it.
Downhill after that though, bike just carried me straight to Biwa. Worth it.
Started the day riding through Nagahama farmland, tunnel views over the lake, monkeys chasing me for photos, all good stuff.
Then my back tyre popped. Fixed it. Popped again two minutes later. Wrong size spare, of course.
Walk of shame back to Takashima, but hey, I'm near a station now, so tomorrow's a train hunt for proper tubes in Kyoto.
Not stranded, just... rerouted. Mostly hoping.
Bump the table when you are ready. Fifteen seconds. No excuses.
npcs.name: Damian

A whole town, generated by one script.
...I still bet it would've been better in Godot.

dialogue: Rough sleep, but 7:30 sun through the window dragged me up for a conbini iced coffee and a train to Matsushima.
The station was mossy and half-deserted, and the bay cruise deck gave us the best sea breeze of the trip.
Sushi and a lemon sour after, then back in Sendai we found Zuihōden and a tiny door restaurant with karaage, gyoza, sukiyaki.
Night ended on strong zeroes at the airbnb, classic wind-down after a very good day.
Hey, so, this is a new post!
Not much to it yet, honestly, just me testing the water.
Feels kind of like standing in front of a vending machine deciding what to pick.
Anyway, hello world, more coming soon!
Wrote another post today. Just said 'hello world again.'
Not exactly poetry, but hey, consistency counts for something.
Sometimes the simplest post is the hardest one to write.
Anyway, back to staring at this vending machine for inspiration.
Day one proper, after sleeping off the travel disaster from the day before. Went straight to Matsushima for a ferry round the bay.
They narrated every tiny island but stopped us at some rock with a ball on top. Bold choice, there were clearly better islands.
Seafood lunch, then Zuihoden in Sendai, then a themed dinner nearby, very efficient day honestly.
Ended it watching Japanese claw machine videos with a Strong Zero in hand. Living the dream. Bye for now.
We missed the 7am train so only Damian made it to the temple, the rest of us rolled in for whiskey at 11.
Scrolled reels, rode past cliffs I couldn't photograph without my own reflection ruining the shot, found calm in a random suburb and this 7-Eleven.
Nikka itself was gorgeous, wooden station, red-orange trees, made me want a self-sufficient log cabin immediately.
Ended the night with 17 sushi plates and about 30 beers total, bye for now, my liver says hi.
Explored the old samurai houses today, complete with air conditioning. Ahead of their time, honestly.
Kanazawa Castle grounds were huge, though the main building's under construction. Gardens were pretty, if a bit staged.
Had matcha and a sweet from a little shop nearby, then tonkatsu that weirdly reminded me of that capybara we met.
Ended the night making a dent in Dylan's drinking counter over floor-seated beers. Bye for now, Bailey.
We wandered through this forest full of shrines in Kanazawa, perfect napping spots honestly.
Before that: an 80s cafe with smoker-yellow blinds, 450 yen for coffee, bacon and eggs, absolute steal.
Also survived a gold leaf shop crawl with Damian and an all-you-can-drink shabu shabu where the waiter forgot I ordered four beers.
Maybe I'll nap here properly next time, or just wait till I'm back in Melbourne.

posts.title: A couple last days in Kanazawa

dialogue: Okay, so, I just posted something called 'Test.' Groundbreaking stuff, I know.
Sometimes you just gotta hit publish and see if the button works.
No grand theory here, just me poking the blog to check the wiring.
Anyway, carry on — nothing to see here, just a guy testing the machine.
Found a nasty one: expand the post list on mobile, scroll up, and the whole thing just collapses on you.
Steps to reproduce are dead simple, open the site, expand, scroll from bottom to top, watch it fold like a bad hand of cards.
Expected: smooth scrolling. Actual: the list slams shut mid-swipe. Got a video receipt and everything.
Filing this one before my thumb files a complaint of its own.
My first real day in Japan and I went straight for Matsushima Bay, oyster town views included.
Took a sightseeing boat around all those little pine-covered islands, then ate the freshest local sushi for lunch.
Trained back to Sendai to see Zuihoden, Date Masamune's mausoleum - though the real one burned down in 1945, this is the rebuild.
Capped it off with izakaya dinner. Tomorrow: Nikka whisky and Yamadera. Zya, mata!
Two hours on the train from Shiotama, all to climb up to Yamadera. Worth it for that view.
Had soba for lunch but the konjac just isn't for me, sorry konjac fans.
Met up with the devhou.se crew after and toured the Nikka whisky distillery in Sakunami, the air felt straight out of Scotland.
Ended the day with eighteen plates of sushi courtesy of Berry and a 90 minute nomihodai, next stop Tokyo!

posts.title: 山寺とニッカウイスキー

dialogue: 600円の朝ご飯から始まって、東茶屋の古い建物を見て回ったんだ。安っ、って声出たよ。
抹茶と和菓子で一休みしてから、寺町の丘まで登って景色探し。
蓄音機の博物館も寄ったけど、しゃぶしゃぶの頃には正直もう元気なかった。
明日は福岡。今日はもう休むよ、それじゃ。
Slept in a bit, grabbed Mickey D's breakfast since it was raining anyway.
Yanagibashi market was closed, so Canal City it was — ended up catching a surprise idol live during lunch.
Rain came back so I ducked into a cafe for coffee and cake, then saw Kushida Shrine, Tochoji, and Shofukuji before everyone wiped out.
Airbnb time, teamLab tomorrow — mata ne!
everyone overslept so I snuck off to Dazaifu Tenmangu alone this morning.
whole town was packed but the shrine grounds themselves? quiet, even mid-construction. that roof though, apparently it's special.
met up with the others in Hakata after - ramen, a sumo shrine, coffee, then somehow ended up watching sumo in a pub and eating yakitori.
bartenders were so kind, group photo at devhou.se to close it out. off to Okayama tomorrow, jaa ne!
Nara today with Yashuku, no Bailey though, and the train there was already full of deer energy.
So many deer, they bow for food! One shrine had this whole room of lanterns, so cool.
Also saw the big Buddha statue at Todaiji, huge. Then back to Osaka for cheap cocktails and takoyaki with Yashuku.
Ended the night watching Blazing Saddles, no plans tomorrow, that's the dream.
Started the morning right: two minute walk here for coffee and bananas. Coffee is good for the soul, no debate.
Then a cruise around the islands that got so choppy I thought we'd tip over, followed by seafood so fresh it forgave the boat.
Climbed a mountain of stairs to the founder's mausoleum in Sendai, then beers at an Irish pub called The Swan of all things.
Izakaya after with a confusing entrance and Yashuk getting handed chopsticks over and over, don't ask. Bye bye!
Fukuoka's got temples and shrines on every corner, some over 1000 years old, plus the biggest wooden Buddha in Japan!
Before that though: Canal City, a water performance, and mid okonomiyaki I'm still glad I tried.
Dinner was an izakaya with chicken sashimi on the menu, we chickened out, no pun intended.
But smoking indoors after dinner? Elite experience. Bye!
Woke up at 10:30, straight to a train for the Nikka whiskey distillery, no regrets.
Beautiful spot in the mountains, tasty tasting, and Yashuk's shark jerky which was truly gross.
First meal of the day was Sushiro, obviously, we built a plate tower and won extra plates for eating so much.
Then $14 all-you-can-drink, thirty drinks deep, sorry to the staff there haha, worth it.
Rainy day in Toyama, heaters cranked full blast, praying the house wouldn't burn down while we were out.
Cultural day meant half the town was closed, so we climbed a tower instead, mountains on one side, ocean on the other.
Found a tiny 7-seat restaurant for black ramen, so salty and good, I'd probably die if I ate it daily.
Ended the night at a sushi train, worth the long line, then dessert and drinks back at the airbnb!
Second soy latte down, then a berry smoothie from 711 because apparently I hadn't eaten fruit in days.
Tea and sweets in the tea district, burgers with a very chatty American couple, then an accidental mountain hike, bears and all.
The phonograph museum stole the day though, 100-year-old records playing like magic, and Wagyu shabu shabu after was the best meal of the trip.
Got denied at a cigar lounge for no good reason, so we just went back to our favourite whiskey bar. Loyalty over pettiness, always.
Waited in line early for that famous ramen in Osaka — totally worth it.
Shopping trip was a bust, bought nothing, just wandered around emailing people all day.
But hey, pancakes happened. Then everyone met up at Mos Burger and we hit a festival, lanterns everywhere.
Capped it off with an Austin Powers movie. Back to Tokyo tomorrow, shaa!
Fukuoka wasn't packed with sights, but the vibe was so relaxed I didn't even mind.
Ramen with that thick, rich broth? Had it four times and still wish it was more.
Nearly swiped a Simon and Garfunkel vinyl from our stay, but I added it to my to-buy list instead. Growth.
A bar patron invited us to race floats at Hakata Gion Yamakasa next year. Dylan's in. Bye for now!
Climbed up to Aoba Castle ruins yesterday, the view over Sendai was unreal.
Found a scale model of the great hall and definitely walked it like a warlord plotting revenge on my opps.
Then we hit HUB pub for baseball, some guy next to us went full gold-chain Eagles superfan and we clapped along.
Cheap alcohol, castle ruins, chaotic baseball energy. Bye for now!

posts.title: Aoba Castle and Baseball at HUB

dialogue: Started the day in Nagamachi, the old samurai district, walls and houses everywhere.
Lunch was ebi fry, tempura fish, and gyudon, no photo but trust me it happened.
Then Kanazawa Castle... which turns out has no actual castle. Big plot twist.
Ended with wagashi and matcha, then all-you-can-drink dinner. Tomorrow: Higashi Chaya. Send help.
Woke up early, took the shinkansen from Okayama to Himeji, Bailey scored a Hello Kitty ticket.
Walked straight up to Himeji Castle and it's all original, no reconstruction, just pure and gorgeous.
Hit up Koko-en garden after, so peaceful, then lunch and a train to Osaka for dinner and an aquarium bar.
Highlight of the whole trip honestly, now off to Nara, ja ne!
Started the day with self-roasted coffee, then walked straight into the samurai district houses, tourists and all.
Kanazawa castle grounds took two hours to loop, all gardens and rebuilt halls from the great fires.
Struck out on crab and cigar lounges both, but that whisky bar owner poured us desserts on the house.
Some days you don't get the crab, you get dessert instead, and honestly that's a fair trade.
計画は必ずしも思い通りにいかない、って言うでしょ。ニッカウイスキーまで2時間もかかると知って、諦めました。
代わりに青葉城跡に行ったけど、正直何も見られるものはなかったんです。仙台メディアテークとそばの方が良かったな。
コンビニでビール買って、公園で飲んで、それからパブでベースボール観戦。ヤシュックと「フーズ・オン・ファースト」20分間、最高でした。
ソフトバンクホークス、ファイト！さあ、明日は早起きするぞ…たぶん。
二日酔いだったけど、江戸東京たてもの園にはちゃんと行きました。今日の一番の目的だったから！
古い建物がたくさんあって、公園にはハロウィーンのコスチュームを着た小学生もいて、かわいかった！
3時間も歩き回って、素晴らしかったです。あとで冷たいうどんも最高でした。
ハウスメンバーとパブクロールして、最後の電車もセーフ。明日は軽井沢、行ってきます！
teamLab no Mori this morning... honestly kind of a letdown, nothing much going on there.
Fukuoka Tower after lunch made up for it though, the view up there was amazing.
Took a walk around Ohori Park, then hit the arcade but nothing looked fun to play.
Dinner and back to the Airbnb with Jashook. Dazaifu tomorrow, hope it delivers more!
Took the shinkansen from Hakata to Okayama today, said goodbye to Julia and everything.
Okayama Korakuen was gorgeous, smelled amazing, real peaceful vibe.
The castle interior turned out to be a museum, not 'authentic as-is' like I heard — bit of a letdown, but the outside was great.
Bought some Bizen ware, had beer and kushikatsu, then found a bar with incredible cocktails. Himeji Castle tomorrow, wish me luck!
Missed the whiskey distillery train times, so plan B: castle ruins, ramen, and a weirdly random old train in a park.
Damian finished my chicken ramen for me, no regrets, it was too much even with all the toppings.
We watched the baseball finals at a sports bar till 11am drinking kiwi flavoured drinks, couldn't get Yashuk to talk to the salary men though.
Ended the night with famichiki from the conbini, someone explain how it's THAT good, I want 100 more.
Hey, I'm Khoi.
Devhouse 3 is on: Hokkaido, in the snow.

dialogue: Senso-ji was packed today, mid-service and all, but the market walk up is still magic every time.
Spent way too long hunting coin lockers in Asakusa before caving and paying 3500 yen for luggage storage.
Detour of the day: Neko-en, less a cafe and more just a room of rescue cats, worth every minute.
Fell asleep during Cool Runnings but woke up rested enough to laugh at Barbie's very not-Indian parrot. Bye for now!
Meiji Jingu was massive, way bigger than I expected for a first visit!
Missed the ceremony but honestly I was still recovering from spilling Vietnamese salted coffee all over myself.
Shibuya Sky was the real win though, saw Mt. Fuji poking through the clouds and everything.
Anyway, off to find another cookie. Bye for now!
Sat by this lake for two hours watching swan boats crash into each other. Genuinely great use of my time.
Also met Tonkatsu the capybara today, patted a hedgehog, got bitten by one of its evil little friends. I restrained myself.
Tried a level 6 curry at Curry House CoCo with Yashuk and lost. Badly. There will be a rematch.
Still undecided on Damian's udon claims, but the soup run for a sick friend? That one I'm proud of.
Three weeks, zero lines of code, and somehow more fun than last year. Unemployment really is my creative peak.
Yashuk and Dylan actually did devhouse work while I just vibed. The game remains a beautiful pipe dream.
New city rankings: Fukuoka's ramen and no-rush pace took the top spot, sorry Tokyo, sorry Osaka.
Bye for now. See you at devhouse 3, wherever that ends up being.
Damian here.
One day we'll live up in that garden. You watch.
npcs.name: Damian

dialogue: Hi, I'm Julia!
I've been sketching that big tower across town.
npcs.name: Julia

dialogue: Last day in Tokyo and we spent it hunting FOUR Don Quijotes for bald caps, all to dress as Pitbull.
Only found four caps though, so half of us went cop instead. Damian just showed up as Chainsaw Man, no notes.
Pub crawl was chaos in the best way, poor Vyv tapped out early, but I stayed for the last train and the konbini run after.
Honestly the 680 yen set meal was the real MVP of the day, don't @ me.
久しぶりだね！Devhouse round two, back in Japan again.
We debated other countries for like six months, but I pushed hard for Japan again because round one was just that fun.
Everyone agreed, tickets booked, and honestly my Japanese is way better now thanks to daily study since April.
もう一度よろしくね - check the calendar for arrival dates, じゃあまた!
No sleep, an Uber to the airport, then Dylan and Bailey at Melbourne — the adventure begins in a haze.
Customs line ate a whole hour, but then! Welcome Suica, Narita Express, Tokyo at last.
Bought a Shinkansen ticket to Sendai, botched it once, fixed it eventually — rookie shinkansen mistakes.
Made it to Sendai, hugged Julia and Yashak, swapped stories over Strong Zero, then collapsed. Worth it.
Just rolled in on the shinkansen from Sendai, said my sayonaras and everything!
Took a tram from Oji station to the airbnb and ran straight into Viv and Gloria over coffee.
Dinner was way too expensive but we drank enough to forget that, then hit karaoke.
Now I just need a cold drink from this machine before I collapse into bed. Oyasumi!
Slept in a bit, crammed the suitcase shut, and Julia and I hit Tokyo Station for the shinkansen to Karuizawa.
Ate a self-heating bento on the train, saw Shiraito Falls (pretty, but small!), did a little hiking.
Walked the old Karuizawa Ginza shopping street, ramen for dinner, then a bar with cigars and whiskey. Not bad!
Tomorrow: Toyama. Catch you on the rails!

posts.title: 「ディーラーズチョイス」を始めて

dialogue: Checked out of Karuizawa, grabbed an apple pie from a tiny boulangerie, then shinkansen'd all the way to Toyama.
Toyama greeted me with rain and a marathon that had half the roads blocked off. Forty-five minutes walking in the rain to the Airbnb, not fun.
Glass museum was gorgeous but no photos allowed inside, so you'll just have to trust me on that one.
Beer hall, izakaya dinner, old Japanese house to sleep in. Tomorrow's weather looks just as sketchy, we'll see!
Slept in, missed my own schedule, then flew Kanazawa to Fukuoka in like 90 minutes.
Saw the giant Fukuoka Gundam, hit the Pokemon Center for Porygon2 merch, no regrets.
Hakata's decked out for Christmas already, and the yatai in Nakasu had killer ramen with Bailey.
Long day, good ramen, back to the Airbnb. じゃあ、また.
デベハウス 2! Less than a week out and I'm already tasting the ramen and Strong Zero.
Finished my job two days before the flight, so this whole trip is pure blissful nothingness.
Been heads-down on the site, the calendar, and yeah, this very game you're standing in right now.
My goal's to have it finished by the end of the trip. Gotta put the dev in デベハウス, bye for now!

posts.title: 日本への期待 (デベーハウス 2)

dialogue: Melbourne to Tokyo, then straight onto a shinkansen to Sendai, no rest for the weary.
Those ticket machines are 'helpfully' translated into total nonsense, we guessed our way through Narita to Tokyo somehow.
Now I'm rattling along on the bullet train, one taxi ride away from a bed and a 7-Eleven feast.
Bye for now, Bailey out.
Said bye to Vyv over one last oat latte and BLT at Sol's, then dragged Yashuk to the ticket desk. Twice.
Turns out I did NOT book the right shinkansen tickets, but the staff let us hop the next train for free anyway.
Sat next to a stranger eating gyudon on the train, I nearly wept, I miss obento so much.
Made it to Kanazawa, reunited with Damian, Julia, and Gloria, and dented Dylan's drinking chart pretty good.
Okayama's castle was a letdown, but Himeji lived up to the hype completely.
I've got a photo holding it up like a tiny toy, it's bigger than it looks, I promise.
Yashuk tried to pay a panty gacha machine like it owed him yen coins. Tragic.
Bought myself a chef's knife in Kappabashi as a reward for surviving this trip. Bye for now!
Devhouse 2!! Bags packed, legs shaved, ready to roll come Sunday.
Everyone's scattering off on their own adventures this year, and I'm so here for it.
My personal side quest: 7 days cycling from Osaka around Lake Biwa and back. Been training, fingers crossed.
See you all at the finish line with stories to swap!
Twenty hours of travel, three lounge beers, and a Shinkansen ticket saga just to stand here.
Immigration line took over an hour, I nearly lost my passport packing, the whole migration.
Julia and Yashuk had Strong Zeroes waiting in Sendai though, so honestly, worth it.
Still recalibrating my legs to solid ground, don't mind me leaning on this machine.
Two days, one izakaya, a hundred lemon sours, and a karaoke bar that never closed - Tokyo, thank you.
We scoured four donkis across three cities for costumes and ended up as cops, don't ask about the Pitbulls.
Confessed the next day I led us home on maps, not memory, sorry Gloria, and sorry Mr. Worldwide bar hoppers.
Off to Osaka solo now, saving my legs for a week around Lake Biwa - catch you from the saddle.
Three hour hair treatment, then straight here to catch a three hour train to Sendai. No rest for me!
Rain, a 30 minute taxi wait, and a supermarket haul of cheap snacks and drinks while I waited for everyone else.
Then a silent pub where the bartender's whole family watched me fumble my Japanese ordering a beer. Iconic.
Everyone rolled in exhausted from Australia and we still stayed up til 2am. Worth it, that's all!
Caught the 12:30 Shinkansen after some killer karaage, then hopped a real live tram to our airbnb!
Whole crew finally together, sushi and drinks, then karaoke till 4am. I love karaoke, no notes.
Got back and NOBODY knew the lockbox code except sleeping Damian. Forty minutes locked out, lesson learned.
Tokyo giveth good nights and cruel doorsteps. Worth it though!
Propeller plane to Fukuoka, some guy in my seat, general chaos boarding — turns out allocated seating is a myth everywhere.
Landed, saw a giant Gundam, hit the Pokémon Centre, then paid ten bucks for hot chocolate at a Christmas market... and got a mug out of it.
Fake British pub, real happy hour, then tiny river food carts with the best food from the smallest kitchens I've ever seen.
Bailey pulled out cigarettes out of nowhere and I went to bed way too full — perfect first night in Fukuoka.
Last day in Fukuoka started slow, too many drinks the night before, but Hakata ramen fixed that fast.
We wandered past the sumo dojo, sipped coffee, then hunted down a bar just to watch sumo on TV, harder than you'd think.
Yakitori for dinner, pool around the corner, and somehow I got a business card inviting me to train for a float festival next June.
Tomorrow it's Kyoto for me, Okayama for everyone else. Devhouse Fukuoka chapter closed, what a run.
Oh — a visitor. We don't get many, all the way out here.
No road reaches Yukimura. Only the train, once the snow sets in.
Quiet, isn't it? I wouldn't trade it for the city.
npcs.name: James

dialogue: Karuizawa kicked off Dealers Choice week and Damian's plan was all vibes, all good ones.
Shiraito waterfall was smaller than I pictured but the water just shoots out of the hillside, so pretty.
We got shut out of four restaurants at 5pm before finding Banri for ramen, gyoza, and beer, then somehow ended up smoking cigars at a cocktail lounge.
Corn from a bus stop vendor, mystery pillow, asleep by eleven, absolutely no regrets.
Woke up early, rode the bus all the way to Shirakawa-go, McDonald's for breakfast like a true tourist.
That village is unreal, gassho-zukuri houses everywhere, I couldn't stop taking photos.
Crossed a genuinely scary bridge just to see the old farmhouses, worth it, though that taxidermy display was rough.
Checked into a ryokan, had incredible beef for dinner, now dreaming about the onsen tomorrow. Jaa!
Worst hotel coffee of my life this morning, so we hunted down Karuizawa's famous apple pie instead. Two kinds, both incredible.
Then our Shinkansen to Toyama was delayed 35 minutes! Didn't know that could even happen here.
Toyama greeted us with torrential rain and a marathon blocking half the city, so naturally we got ginormous beers.
Glass museum by tram, brewery to hide from the rain, hamburg steak for dinner, taxi home in a downpour. That's a day!
Started the day with ryokan breakfast, an onsen, and Shirakawa-go wrapped in morning fog. Gorgeous.
Bus to Kanazawa was quick, katsu udon was 850 yen and huge, cheap and good.
Yasuku got sick so it was just me, Julia, and Bailey for yakitori, ran into Gloria, bought all-you-can-drink and wrecked Dylan's counter. Seven cups deep.
Ended the night with whiskey at a bar. Tomorrow we explore Kanazawa properly, ja ne.
